name: VK2735

lead: VK2735 is a weekly injectable (and oral form in trials) that activates the GLP-1 and GIP receptors, like tirzepatide. Viking Therapeutics is running phase 3 trials for obesity.
In a 13-week phase 2 study, people lost 9 to 15% of body weight on it versus about 2% on placebo.

paras: It activates GLP-1 and GIP receptors to reduce appetite and affect metabolism, as other incretin-based weight-loss drugs do.
Safety is still being assessed in phase 3. It is not approved, and the 13-week trial was short, so long-term effects are unknown.

lead: VK2735 is an investigational dual agonist of the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptors, developed by Viking Therapeutics for weight management. It is being tested as a weekly subcutaneous injection and as a daily oral formulation, and is not approved as a medicine. [1][2][3][4]
It works on the same pair of receptors as tirzepatide, which is already approved. Reviews discuss new co-agonists of this type as more potent weight-loss drugs than GLP-1 agonism alone. [5]

In a 13-week phase 2 trial in adults with obesity or overweight, mean weight loss ranged from 9.1% to 14.7% depending on dose, versus 1.7% with placebo. [1] Phase 3 trials started in 2025, and there is no evidence of use outside medical studies for appearance purposes.
infobox: Weekly subcutaneous injection; oral form in trials

paras: Phase 1: a phase 1 safety and tolerability study (NCT05203237) in 92 participants began in December 2021 and has been completed. [2]

Phase 2 (injection): the VENTURE trial was a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study of weekly subcutaneous VK2735 in adults with obesity or overweight and at least one weight-related condition, excluding diabetes. Conducted from August 2023 to February 2024, it reported mean weight reductions of 9.2 kg at the lowest dose and 14.6 kg at the highest, against 1.8 kg for placebo. [1][3] In the active groups, 93% of participants lost at least 5% of body weight, compared with 12% on placebo. [1]
Phase 2 (oral): a phase 2 trial of oral VK2735 (NCT06828055) enrolling 280 participants has been completed. [4]

Phase 3: registered phase 3 trials include a weight management study of about 4,500 participants, VANQUISH 2 in people with type 2 diabetes, and the oral SUNRISE 1 and 2 trials that were due to start in late 2026. [6][7][8][9] A further phase 1 study in obese adults without comorbidities is recruiting. [10]

The VENTURE trial report lists common adverse events, which the available abstract does not detail; the trial was a short 13-week study. [1] Review authors discussing next-generation GLP-1 co-agonists note that cardiac effects of such drugs remain an area needing more research. [5]

timeline.event: Phase 2 VENTURE trial begins in August. [3]
Phase 3 trials begin; an oral phase 2 trial starts in December 2024. [4][6][7]
